title: XTP service addressing and multicast for Memory Fabric
summary: When XTP is qualified, named service FIRST admission, KEY/ROUTE contexts and carrier selection remain below Memory Fabric. Multicast is capability-specific, not an implicit property of a named service.
invariants: ServiceDescriptor maps memory.block.read / memory.block.locate / memory.block.invalidate canonical names to local operational classes and logical XTP peers; physical addresses remain only in XTP routing.

One-to-many XTP multicast can disseminate discovery and invalidation coordination only to an authenticated, policy-admitted, explicitly scoped receiver population. XTP quorum is not a memory lease or block commit.
XTP named-service unicast and multicast address bindings remain separate at dev25. Do not advertise verified combined service-addressed reliable multicast until exercised.

L2 EtherType 0x817D is for proven shared Ethernet domains; native IPv4 protocol 36 for qualified MU paths; XTP/UDP when policy permits. Never infer cross-cloud Layer-2 or native protocol-36 reachability.
XTP chooses a physical path; Connect Selector and Socket Selector remain independent higher-level/service choices. No compulsory XTP dependency for ordinary standalone Memory Fabric use.
Current XTP v0.1-dev34 supports encrypted named-service messages; Memory Fabric uses live active/retiring key identity, not XTP KEY or caller label, for read access.
Protected multicast group-key admission is not qualified by dev34; no confidential Memory Fabric publication via unprotected multicast.

provenance.claim: ServiceDescriptor-based named XTP FIRST and admission mapping.
Unicast native rate-capable socket and distinct multicast socket implementations.
